profile.name: Yiran Zhang
profile.intro: I work on AI agent evaluation. My research background spans adversarial testing, uncertainty monitoring, and human–machine collaboration, alongside hands-on work with robotic systems.
profile.context: My research at Nanyang Technological University has explored how to expose failures, assess reliability, and support decisions under uncertainty in autonomous systems.
profile.availability: I am also interested in opportunities in robotics and embodied intelligence.

research.title: OOD-Aware Joint Prediction and Planning for Autonomous Driving with Contrastive Learning and Reconstruction-Based Filtering
research.summary: A new joint prediction-and-planning (PnP) algorithm that explicitly accounts for the limited coverage of its training data. Trained on Argoverse 2 and evaluated across five datasets in closed-loop tests, including adversarial scenarios.

research.title: A Robust Guardian for Autonomous Driving with Game-Theoretic and Diffusion Counterfactuals
research.summary: Game-theoretic and diffusion counterfactuals train a guardian to detect unfamiliar situations and support contingency re-planning. Evaluation covers multiple datasets, traffic environments, and three planner types.
research.highlight: A monitor that knows its own uncertainty.

research.title: Adversarial Traffic Scene Generation Considering Harm, Rarity, and Ambiguity for Autonomous Driving Testing
research.summary: Adversarial scenes target harm, rarity, and ambiguity, combining game-theoretic interactions with uncertainty-based objectives. Evaluations test how effectively these scenes expose vulnerabilities in both optimization-based and learning-based planners.

research.title: A Planner-agnostic Monitor for Behaviour Feasibility of Autonomous Vehicles Using a Bayesian Discriminator
research.venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
research.summary: MonitorGAN uses a Bayesian discriminator to assess plan feasibility and estimate its own uncertainty, without real outlier exposure during training. Cross-dataset experiments cover learning-based, polynomial-based, and optimization-based planners.

research.title: Interactive Prediction and Decision-Making for Autonomous Vehicles: Online Active Learning with Traffic Entropy Minimization
research.venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
research.summary: Online learning updates a fixed predictor as new interactions unfold, while traffic-entropy minimization encourages more predictable decisions. Human-in-the-loop and cross-dataset experiments evaluate reliability under uncertain road-user behaviour.

research.title: Socially-Compliant Hierarchical Human-Vehicle Collaboration with Multimodal Haptic Steering
research.venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
research.summary: A shared-driving framework combines interaction-aware prediction, human guidance, and haptic steering. Human-in-the-loop experiments assess human–machine conflict and safety under dynamically allocated control authority.
research.highlight: Connecting human decisions with control feedback.

research.title: Human-Machine Cooperative Decision-making and Planning for Automated Vehicles Using Spatial Projection of Hand Gestures
research.summary: Hand gestures are projected onto the road to guide cooperative decision-making and planning. Experiments compare driving performance and physical and mental workload with conventional manual guidance.
research.highlight: High-level guidance through a visual interface.

research.title: Shutoko Highway: Autonomous Driving & Human–Machine Interface
research.summary: An integrated autonomous-driving and human–machine interface demonstration. The project investigates situations in which passengers do not trust the driving algorithm, with the aim of informing more personalized driving behaviour. The work includes the driving algorithm and the interaction interfaces.

research.title: Human-like Interactive Behavior Generation for Autonomous Vehicles: A Bayesian Game-theoretic Approach with Turing Test
research.summary: A Bayesian game model captures road-user interaction under uncertain intentions, including probing behaviour. Simulation experiments and Turing tests evaluate the human-likeness of the generated scenes.

projects.title: Robot Throwing & Catching
projects.summary: A robotic-arm demonstration exploring how throwing and catching a tennis ball can extend manipulation beyond the arm’s physical reach. Developed independently.

projects.title: Robot Teleoperation Interface
projects.summary: A demonstration of an interface for remotely guiding a robotic arm.
